summary: Alexander Studholme is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin around 1995 to 2001.

Alexander W. Macdonald was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1980) and Paris Nanterre University (Professor, ~1974–1989), alongside affiliations with the Musée de l'Homme, Kailash, and the University of Paris.

Alexander Wynne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and at Oxford under Richard Gombrich (DPhil 2000–2003), later serving as a Junior Research Fellow at St John's College (2002–2006).
Alexander Yiannopoulos is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under Karin Myers, Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, Jay L. Garfield, and others.

Alexander von Humboldt studied at European University Viadrina, Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and the University of Jena, where he also held an academic post.
Alexander von Rospatt is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at UCL and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen) and held positions at Leipzig, Vienna, and UC Berkeley.

Alexander von Staël-Holstein was an Indologist and Sinologist who earned his doctorate at Halle under Richard Pischel. He served at Saint Petersburg, was professor at Peking University (1918–1929), and founded and directed the Sino-Indian Institute (~1927–1937).
Alexandra David-Néel was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and under Philippe Édouard Foucaux and Kazi Dawa Samdup.

Alexandra van der Geer works in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, and Paul Y. Sondaar, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1815–1827). He taught at the Lycée Charlemagne (~1817–1835) and held positions as inspecteur at the Académie de Paris and member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

Alexis Sanderson is an Indologist who studied at Oxford and under Swami Lakshman Joo. At the University of Oxford, he served as Lecturer in Sanskrit (~1977–1992) and Professor (~1992–2015), alongside a fellowship at All Souls College.

Alf Hiltebeitel was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner, and held a professorship at George Washington University from 1968.
Alf Sommerfelt was a linguist who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924 and served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She studied at Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giuseppe Tucci, as well as under Louis Renou, Jacques Bacot, and Marcelle Lalou, later teaching Sanskrit at the University of Rome in 1952.

Alfred Bloom was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Harvard, and served as professor of religion at Oregon (1961–1970) and Hawaiʻi (1970–1986), later becoming Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1986–1994).
Alfred Chilton Pearson was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Highgate School, King's College School, and Christ's College, where he was taught by John Peile (~1879–1883).

Alfred Cooper Woolner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of Oriental College (~1903–1936) and held posts at the University of the Punjab, serving as Vice Chancellor from 1928 to 1936.

Alfred Cort Haddon worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at King's College London and Christ's College, and held posts at the University of Cambridge (1879–1880; 1900–1926) and the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901).
Alfred Edward Housman was an academic who studied at St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881) and later held a post at University College London (~1892–1911).

Alfred Ernout was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1972), University of Paris (~1927–1944), and Collège de France (1941–1951).
